text:
matt: starting an RFC thread for the compatibility surface + fallback launch scope. goal: define must-have acceptance criteria, edge cases, and a prioritized rollout plan. cc @anna for product, @raj for infra.

anna: quick question — do we treat dedicated vs hosted differently for fallbacks? customers expect isolation on Dedicated.

sofia: yes, Dedicated can't automatically fallback to shared hosted variants without explicit config. acceptance: fallback must be opt-in for Dedicated. :white_check_mark:

raj: infra notes: we need a compatibility matrix for model variants (quantized vs full-fp), tokenization differences, and region affinity. if a fallback crosses regions we need data residency check and optional user prompt.

kevin: prioritization suggestion: 1) host-host fallbacks within same region (low-risk), 2) model-variant fallbacks same infra (e.g., fp32 -> int8), 3) cross-region fallbacks (needs compliance signoff), 4) Dedicated->Hosted (enters data isolation constraints).

matt: acceptance criteria draft: 
- fallback routing policy returns a compatible variant that matches output schema and tokenization.
- latency delta for fallback path bounded: p95 latency increase <= 2x baseline or <= 300ms, whichever smaller.
- fallbacks should maintain configured SLO for availability (no more than X% error spike)
- for Dedicated customers, fallback must be disabled by default and require explicit opt-in.

anna: add business criteria: fallback should reduce error-rate driven incidents by >= 50% in first 30 days for tiered traffic. and document billing impact (token delta).

sofia: edge cases we must call out: 
- partial-response: model returns truncated sequence; should we re-route to a longer-context variant or just surface partial and mark degraded?
- incompatible output (different special tokens or function-calling signatures) -> must reject fallback and surface a structured error.

raj: technical edge-case list: 
- KV cache mismatch across model variants -> must flush per-request or prefer cold-start safe fallbacks.
- quantized variants may drop accuracy on certain prompts; require per-model quality tags in catalog.

matt: propose acceptance tests: 
- automated harness that sends 1k representative prompts, forces primary variant to 503 and asserts fallback responses meet schema and satisfy quality thresholds (per-eval metric).
- latency and cost regression tests comparing primary vs fallback.

kevin: dependencies: model catalog must expose compatibility labels (tokenizer id, function schema version, quality score). rollout tool must support route rules with tier+region predicates.

anna: timeline ask from sales: need a beta for a few enterprise customers in 6 weeks. is that feasible?

raj: feasible if we scope beta to same-region host-host + model-variant within same pool. cross-region + Dedicated opt-ins should come later.

sofia: metrics to collect in beta: fallback rate, success rate (schema + basic eval), p50/p95 latency, token cost delta, customer-visible errors. also record case-id when fallback triggered for postmortem.

matt: suggested rollout plan (short): 
1) RFC + acceptance criteria sign-off this week.
2) infra & catalog changes (compat labels) week 1-2.
3) minimal routing rules + canary (host-host same region) week 3.
4) invited beta with 3 customers week 4-6.

kevin: what is minimal policy DSL we need to start? something like:
```
policy: {
  match: { tier: "standard", region: "us-west-2" },
  primary: "gptx-v1-fp32",
  fallback_order: ["gptx-v1-int8", "gptx-v0-legacy"],
  constraints: { tokenizer: "utf8-v2", functions: "v2" }
}
```

anna: looks good. add explicit default: no cross-region by default.

raj: security note: logging fallback events must redact prompt content for PII. store only hashes and metadata.

matt: next steps: anna to sign product acceptance, raj to scope infra work items and list trunk PRs, sofia to author test harness and evaluation thresholds. I'll assemble a short PRD and post link.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for routing-service v2.1 in us-west-2 tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

kevin: one last thing — define rollback condition: if fallback success rate < 90% or p95 latency > 2x baseline for 15m window, auto rollback.

matt: noted. i'll put rollback thresholds into the PRD. thanks all. :rocket:
